# Tool reference

Every tool works on the **active workspace**. Tool failures come back as a result with `isError: true` and a message naming the problem; an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error (`-32602`). JSON results are sent as text and, to clients on protocol 2025-06-18 or later, also as `structuredContent` (a top-level array is wrapped as `{"items": [...]}`).

| Tool | Summary | Hints |
|---|---|---|
| [`push_dialogue`](#push_dialogue) | Push a dialogue turn | writes |
| [`store_memory`](#store_memory) | Store a fact | writes |
| [`query_memory`](#query_memory) | Search short-term memory | writes, idempotent |
| [`recall_ltm`](#recall_ltm) | Search the long-term archive | read-only, idempotent |
| [`remember_document`](#remember_document) | File a document | writes |
| [`workspace_current`](#workspace_current) | Active workspace | read-only, idempotent |
| [`workspace_list`](#workspace_list) | List workspaces | read-only, idempotent |
| [`workspace_create`](#workspace_create) | Create a workspace | writes, idempotent, pinned: hidden |
| [`workspace_switch`](#workspace_switch) | Switch workspace | writes, idempotent, pinned: hidden |
| [`workspace_export`](#workspace_export) | Export a workspace | read-only, idempotent |
| [`workspace_delete`](#workspace_delete) | Delete a workspace | **destructive**, idempotent, pinned: hidden |
| [`inspect`](#inspect) | Inspect memory | read-only, idempotent |

Tools marked *pinned: hidden* are not listed when the server runs with `[mcp] allow_workspace_switch = false`: such a server stays on its startup workspace and can't reach any other one. Calling them anyway returns an `isError` result explaining why.

## Memory tools

### push_dialogue

**Push a dialogue turn** — Push the latest conversation turn to short-term memory. The turn is archived, facts are extracted from it (when a chat LLM is configured), and the optimized context window is returned: {summary, recent_messages, relevant_facts, learning_error?, warnings?}. Extraction problems are reported in the result, not as a failure; don't retry because of them (the turn is already archived).

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | string | yes | The conversation's session id. (≤ 256 bytes) |
| `new_message` | string | yes | The new dialogue turn. (≤ 65,536 bytes) |
| `ccl` | string | no | Cognitive context layer. Defaults to 'reality'. (≤ 256 bytes) |

### store_memory

**Store a fact** — Store one crucial fact in short-term memory immediately, bypassing the extraction pipeline.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fact_text` | string | yes | The factual statement to store. (≤ 16,384 bytes) |
| `ccl` | string | no | Cognitive context layer. Defaults to 'reality'. (≤ 256 bytes) |
| `tags` | string[] | no | Tags for categorizing the fact. (≤ 64 items) |

### query_memory

**Search short-term memory** — Search SHORT-TERM working memory (recent, decaying facts) for relevant context. Hybrid keyword + semantic search; returns facts (best first) with 1-hop connections and temporal bounds, and each direct hit's fused score when the server enables scores. Reading a fact reinforces it (its relevance is restored and its decay clock restarts). For the permanent document archive, use recall_ltm.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | What to look for. (≤ 4,096 bytes) |
| `ccl_filter` | string[] | no | Cognitive layers to search. Defaults to ['reality']. (≤ 32 items) |
| `k` | integer | no | Max results to return; larger values are clamped. Defaults to 10. (1–100) |
| `time_filter` | object | no | Optional temporal bounds. (fields `after`, `before`) |

### recall_ltm

**Search the long-term archive** — Search the PERMANENT long-term archive (all filed documents and notes) by meaning and by the words of each document's full text, fused into one ranking. Reference-returning: each hit carries the document's dataId, provenance, ancestor concepts and vector distance (and its fused score, when the server enables scores), so you can fetch the original. The primary tool for finding a document, receipt, letter, or report.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | What to look for in the archive: a phrase, topic, merchant, or document description. (≤ 4,096 bytes) |
| `k` | integer | no | Max results to return; larger values are clamped. Defaults to 10. (1–50) |

### remember_document

**File a document** — File a document or note into the PERMANENT long-term archive: it is summarized (if a chat LLM is configured), embedded, and placed under the best-matching concept. Returns {data_id, leaf_id, concept_path, updated, summarized}. Passing the data_id of an existing document replaces that document (upsert).

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: false`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes | The document text. (≤ 524,288 bytes) |
| `data_id` | string | no | Stable id for upserts. Omitted: a new id is minted. (≤ 256 bytes) |
| `tags` | string[] | no | Optional tags. (≤ 64 items) |
| `title` | string | no | Human-facing title. Defaults to the first line of text. (≤ 4,096 bytes) |

## Workspace tools

### workspace_current

**Active workspace** — The active workspace: {name, path, stm_bytes, ltm_bytes, active}. Each workspace is a completely separate memory (its own STM and LTM stores); every memory tool reads and writes the active one.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

No arguments.

### workspace_list

**List workspaces** — All workspaces with their store sizes, sorted by name; the active one has active=true.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

No arguments.

### workspace_create

**Create a workspace** — Create a new, empty workspace (a separate memory) and return its info. Does not switch to it.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Workspace name: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) |

### workspace_switch

**Switch workspace** — Make another existing workspace active and return its info. Its stores are opened and the session buffers start empty; all memory tools then read and write that workspace.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Workspace name: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) |

### workspace_export

**Export a workspace** — JSON dump of a workspace's STM facts and LTM document leaves (each with its full text): {workspace, stm_facts, ltm_leaves}. Defaults to the active workspace.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | no | Workspace name: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) |

### workspace_delete

**Delete a workspace** — DESTRUCTIVE: permanently delete a workspace and all of its memory. Requires confirm equal to name. The active workspace cannot be deleted; switch away first.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Workspace name: 1-64 chars of a-z, 0-9, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit. (pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`) |
| `confirm` | string | yes | Must equal name, to confirm the deletion. |

## Inspection

### inspect

**Inspect memory** — Read-only look inside the active workspace's memory (a "CT scan"); never calls an LLM. Pick what to see with `view`: stats (full metrics of both stores), health (compact summary), stm (list STM facts), ltm_map (top layers of the LTM concept tree), node (one LTM node with its children and documents), subtree (a branch of the LTM tree), trace (where a document lives, by data_id), placement (distance calibration for the placement thresholds). Arguments that belong to another view are rejected.

Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: false`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `view` | `stats` \| `health` \| `stm` \| `ltm_map` \| `node` \| `subtree` \| `trace` \| `placement` | yes | What to inspect. |
| `child_limit` | integer | no | [node] Max children/leaves to return. Defaults to 50. (1–500) |
| `child_offset` | integer | no | [node] Children/leaves to skip (pagination). Defaults to 0. (≥ 0) |
| `contains` | string | no | [stm] Case-insensitive substring the fact text must contain. (≤ 4,096 bytes) |
| `data_id` | string | no | [trace] The document's data_id (required by this view). (≤ 256 bytes) |
| `depth` | integer | no | [ltm_map, subtree] Number of layers. Defaults to 3 for ltm_map, 2 for subtree. (1–10) |
| `id` | integer | no | [node, subtree] The LTM node id (required by these views). |
| `limit` | integer | no | [stm] Max facts to return. Defaults to 20. (1–500) |
| `offset` | integer | no | [stm] Facts to skip (pagination). Defaults to 0. (≥ 0) |
| `sample` | integer | no | [placement] Number of document leaves to probe. Defaults to 30. (1–500) |
| `status` | `active` \| `archived` | no | [stm] Only facts with this status. |
| `summary_max_chars` | integer | no | [node] Cap each summary to this many chars (0 = full). Defaults to 200. (0–100,000) |

| `view` | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `stats` | none | Full metrics snapshot of both stores: STM active/archived counts, average relevance, decay histogram; LTM tree nodes, leaves, edges, inbox size, orphan leaves, max depth; store sizes. |
| `health` | none | Compact summary: STM/LTM counts, orphan leaves, store sizes, feeder_lag (-1 = unknown here; Kafka mode publishes live lag on its metrics topic). |
| `stm` | `limit`, `offset`, `status`, `contains` | STM facts, most relevant first, with score, status, support count, layer, last access and data_id. Paged, with optional status and substring filters. |
| `ltm_map` | `depth` | The top concept layers of the LTM tree (a table of contents). |
| `node` | `id`, `child_limit`, `child_offset`, `summary_max_chars` | One LTM node: summary, parents, children and document leaves (paged), plus child_count / leaf_count totals. |
| `subtree` | `id`, `depth` | A branch of concepts below an LTM node. |
| `trace` | `data_id` | Where a document lives: its LTM leaf and ancestor branch, and how many STM facts carry its data_id. |
| `placement` | `sample` | {thresholds, probes}: the effective distance thresholds (including placement_min_margin) with their source (config / model_default / fallback), and for a sample of document leaves the nearest and runner-up concepts (never the root) with their distances, the margin between them, and the placement decision under the current settings (file / inbox_too_far / inbox_ambiguous). Used to tune the placement cutoff and margin. |
